sections.title: RAG quality is decided by retrieval, not by the model

blocks.heading: Parsing and chunking
paragraphs: Tables, headings, scanned PDFs and long contracts each need different handling. We design chunking around document structure so retrieved passages carry enough context to answer the question.

blocks.heading: Retrieval you can measure
paragraphs: We build an evaluation set from real questions and measure retrieval recall, answer faithfulness and citation accuracy before launch — then track the same metrics in production so changes never silently degrade quality.

blocks.heading: Access control and compliance
paragraphs: Retrieval respects the permissions of the person asking, so users only see answers drawn from documents they are allowed to read. Regulated deployments add audit logging and compliance documentation.

items.question: What is a RAG system?
items.answer: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is an architecture that retrieves relevant passages from your own knowledge sources and gives them to a language model, so answers are grounded in your content and can cite their sources instead of relying only on what the model learned in training.

items.question: How much does RAG development cost?
items.answer: RAG development typically costs $25,000–$300,000. A single knowledge base Q&A system runs $25,000–$55,000, multi-source RAG $40,000–$90,000, agentic RAG $55,000–$130,000 and multi-tenant enterprise platforms $100,000–$300,000.

items.question: How long does it take to build a RAG system?
items.answer: A single knowledge base Q&A system takes 8–14 weeks. Multi-source and hybrid search systems take 10–18 weeks, and enterprise platforms 20–36 weeks.

items.question: What does RAG cost to run each month?
items.answer: Ongoing costs for LLM API, vector database, embeddings and compute typically total $600–$1,500 per month at small scale, $1,000–$3,300 at medium scale and $2,500–$10,000 at enterprise scale.

items.question: Should we use RAG or fine-tuning?
items.answer: RAG is the better fit when answers must come from changing, proprietary knowledge and cite sources. Fine-tuning is better for teaching a model a style, format or narrow task. Many production systems combine both.

items.question: Who owns the RAG system?
items.answer: You do — source code, ingestion pipelines, vector indices, evaluation datasets and documentation are transferred at completion.

sections.heading: Ground your AI in the knowledge your business already has
sections.text: Tell us what questions people need answered and where the knowledge lives. An engineer will reply within one business day with a recommended RAG architecture and budget range.
